raw_case_text:
A 32-year old female with Acute Promyelocytic Leukaemia (APML), previously treated by autogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), presented with pancytopaenia and evidence of relapsed disease. She was started on IV Arsenic and All-trans Retinoic Acid (ATRA) as a bridge to allogeneic HSCT, but became pyrexial and increasingly oxygen-dependent. Serial chest radiographs followed by thoracic Computed Tomography (CT) scanning on Day 28 revealed progressive, extensive ground glass opacification (see Fig. 1(a)). Repeat CT imaging on Day 44 demonstrated additional intrapulmonary mass lesions (see Fig. 1(b)). Galactomannan titres (Aspergillus Antigen Index Value 0.89) and subsequent bronchial lavage and pleural fluid cultures would later confirm IPA secondary to Aspergillus Flavus.
The patient's illness was complicated by a left-sided tension pneumothorax on Day 56. This prompted intercostal drain (ICD) insertion (12F, Rocket Medical ) and ICU admission. Despite appropriate antifungal and supportive therapies and a second ICD (16F, Rocket Medical ) the patient's lung failed to re-expand. Invasive mechanical ventilation was avoided and the patient managed with high-level oxygen supplementation. Digital thoracic drainage units (Thopaz , Medela, Switzerland) demonstrated a consistent PAL in excess of 2000 ml/min, likely due to a ruptured fungal cavity in the lingular subsegment, which was demonstrated on a third CT scan on Day 96 (see Fig. 2). The patient was deemed unsuitable for thoracic surgical intervention due to excessive risk. Since EBVs are not a licensed treatment for PAL in the UK National Health Service, applications for funding and internal clinical governance board approval were submitted on compassionate grounds and approved.
Flexible bronchoscopy was initially attempted in ICU under conscious sedation but was poorly tolerated. General anaesthesia was therefore induced and the trachea intubated with manual IPPV applied prior to bronchoscopy. A single 4.0 mm EBV (Zephyr 4.0 , Pulmonx Inc. Neuchatel, Switzerland) was deployed into the lingular segmental bronchus after inflation of a balloon catheter at this site resulted in complete cessation of air leak. This effect was carefully verified prior to EBV deployment using live air leak data displayed on the Thopaz  unit attached to her 16F axillary drain. This was corroborated by cessation of bubbling through the anterior 12F drain circuit, which was attached to wall suction set at -20 cm H20 pressure. The patient was extubated within one hour of EBV deployment. The 16F axillary ICD was removed 12 h later having demonstrated no measurable air leak on the Thopaz  device since the procedure.
Repeat CT imaging 2 weeks later demonstrated satisfactory positioning of the EBV and significant lung re-expansion (see Fig. 3). The remaining 12F ICD was removed 2 weeks later, following a 48-h period during which no measurable air leak had been detected on Thopaz . The patient expectorated the EBV 3 weeks later without any adverse effect and was eventually discharged home following a 5-month admission. Prolonged antifungal therapy and continuing IV Arsenic and ATRA are planned. Her most recent bone marrow aspirate demonstrates continued molecular remission and she has been referred for allogeneic HSCT.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 32-year-old female with relapsed acute promyelocytic leukemia developed persistent fever, progressive oxygen dependence, and a left-sided tension pneumothorax with a persistent air leak during salvage arsenic trioxide and all-trans retinoic acid therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Previously treated with autologous HSCT for APML, the patient presented with pancytopenia and relapsed disease and was started on intravenous arsenic trioxide and ATRA as a bridge to allogeneic HSCT. She became febrile and increasingly hypoxic with progressive pulmonary infiltrates and masses on day 28 and day 44 CT scans due to invasive pulmonary aspergillosis. On day 56, she developed a left-sided tension pneumothorax requiring ICU admission and two intercostal drains (12F and 16F), complicated by failure of lung re-expansion and a high-volume persistent air leak (>2,000 mL/min) from a ruptured lingular fungal cavity.
subjective.past_medical_history: Relapsed acute promyelocytic leukemia (APML) status post prior autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, progressive hypoxemia/dyspnea, and acute left tension pneumothorax.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile and oxygen-dependent; developed clinical signs of left-sided tension pneumothorax on day 56 with a continuous air leak exceeding 2,000 mL/min on digital thoracic drainage (Thopaz) despite two chest tubes (12F anterior and 16F axillary).
objective.routine_investigations: Presented with pancytopenia; serial chest radiographs showed progressive pulmonary opacities and subsequent left tension pneumothorax. Follow-up bone marrow aspirate after salvage therapy confirmed molecular remission of APML.
objective.advanced_workup: Thoracic CT on day 28 showed extensive ground-glass opacification, day 44 CT demonstrated intrapulmonary mass lesions, and day 96 CT identified a ruptured fungal cavity in the lingular subsegment causing the bronchopleural fistula. Serum galactomannan antigen was positive (index 0.89), and bronchoalveolar lavage and pleural fluid cultures grew Aspergillus flavus. Under general anesthesia, balloon occlusion of the lingular segmental bronchus completely halted the air leak, and a single 4.0-mm Zephyr endobronchial valve (EBV) was deployed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Proven cavitary invasive pulmonary aspergillosis caused by Aspergillus flavus complicated by a ruptured lingular cavity, left tension pneumothorax, and high-output persistent bronchopleural air leak (>2,000 mL/min) in a patient with relapsed APML, confirmed by positive galactomannan (index 0.89), serial thoracic CTs, and BAL and pleural fluid cultures growing A. flavus. Deemed unfit for thoracic surgery, she was treated with prolonged antifungal therapy and compassionate-use bronchoscopic deployment of a 4.0-mm Zephyr endobronchial valve into the lingular segmental bronchus, which immediately arrested the air leak, allowed removal of the 16F drain at 12 hours and the 12F drain at 2 weeks, and achieved lung re-expansion; she spontaneously expectorated the EBV 3 weeks later without recurrence and was discharged in molecular remission as a candidate for allogeneic HSCT.
